AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: Pregnancy increases the risk of gender-based violence, considered an underdiagnosed public health problem.

AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: To determine the association between the situation of possible gender-based violence in the pregnant woman and variables related to pregnancy, labor, puerperium, and newborn health.

AbstractText.Label: PARTICIPANTS
AbstractText.content: 141 pregnant women in which information is collected sociodemographic variables and data related to pregnancy, labor, and puerperium were gathered by interview and from clinical records. Comparisons of means and logistic regression analyses were performed, calculating crude and adjusted odds ratios.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: The study included 141 women; 44 in a situation of possible abuse required more medication during labor (p=0.018), had less early skin contact with their newborn (p=0.021) and more non-reassuring cardiotocography traces (p=0.012), and reported greater pain during labor (p=0.013). The children of the mothers in this situation had a lower mean Apgar score (p˂0.059), less frequently began breastfeeding early (p=0.008), and had higher risk of low birth weight (p˂0.001).

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: The situation of possible abuse in pregnant women may negatively affect their pregnancy, their pain and need for medication during labor, and other newborn health indicators, among other health parameters.
